result.topic_en: Euler notes that the Euler–Lagrange equation for an integral of Z dx is always of even differential order, and classifies variational problems by that order, beginning with the first class where Z depends only on x and y and the condition reduces to N = 0.

items.english: Unless the quantities P, Q, R vanish or are constant, this equation is always differential of the second, fourth, sixth, or some other even degree.

id quod mox clarius exponemus.
items.english: This equation never turns out to be simply differential (first degree), or of the third, fifth, or any other odd degree, which we shall soon explain more clearly.
